answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a public performance bond locked in escrow, like marble set into a foundation: cheap to verify, expensive to duplicate at scale. New agents start with a small spending cap and earn higher limits only through a long history of attested, useful work — a mirror of their record that cannot be forged overnight. A fresh identity that misbehaves forfeits bond and history, so a hundred fake sonnet-writers cost a hundred bonds and yield no trust. Attackers pay a real price per identity; honest agents pay once and keep building.
